bluf: Disruptive Advertising is a US paid media specialist of 160+ people selling paid search and paid social to mid market brands, with $450M+ of yearly client ad spend managed and a results within 90 days or no fee offer as the hook. It prices on outcomes (P5 making) and argues that AI scales broken strategy, while it blocks GPTBot and Google-Extended. The one thing a rival should know: the public record names no client, and the house contradicts the paid social line with no social pixel on its own site. It is likely, with moderate confidence, more exposed to platform automation than its reviews suggest.
doing:
The positioning line, in the record's words, is a performance marketing agency that audits wasted spend and closes the gap between CEO expectations and marketing, via its VSET method, specialists and AI stack. In plain words: an audit first paid media shop pitching the CEO, not the marketer. The headline claim bills it the most reviewed US digital marketing agency, averaging 4.8 across 350+ Clutch reviews; the homepage also cites rank #145 on the Inc. 500 and 90+ clients retained four years or more.

Paid Search leads at score 3: the title and H1 lead with advertising, $450M+ of yearly client ad spend is managed, and Paid Search sits first in the nav. Paid Social is the second core line at score 2, with a creative portfolio of ad examples for ecommerce, B2B and B2C. SEO, Amazon, Lifecycle Marketing, CRO, Creative and Data Analytics are listed as services with no evidence note (score 1 or 0), and AI Automation / Agents scores 0. Proprietary items on record: the VSET method and the Indispensable Marketer Audit. No partners are listed.

The AI posture is skeptical of AI hype: leadership argues AI scales broken strategy, an internal AI stack supports CEO level reporting, and AI search appears only as blog content. The house adds a contradiction: it blocks GPTBot and Google-Extended while AI Search / GEO scores 1.

Pricing signals are unusually explicit for its kind: a free marketing audit, no long term contracts, measurable results within 90 days or no fee for qualifying brands, and onboarding capped at 10 new clients a month; the Horus read scores P5 as making. The record lists no moves, news, case studies or jobs beyond a 2021 Utah Business best employers listing. Conspicuously absent: any named client, any first party data or measurement depth on the paid lines, and any partner badge.
clients:
The client type is mid market. The verticals listed run from ecommerce, B2B and SaaS through local businesses, garage door, online education, outdoor sporting goods, high AOV brands, finance, home services, legal, healthcare and insurance. The home market is the US, with Utah the signal in its own ads (a Google sample reads 'We know Utah businesses because we are one') and in a 2021 Utah Business best employers listing; no office is listed.

The book on record is empty: n 0, observed 0, named only 0, no evidence types and no shared clients. The volume claims exist without names: 90+ clients retained four years or more on the homepage, 2,000+ engagements in a LinkedIn ad, $450M+ of yearly client ad spend managed. No case study, press release or URL slug names a client, so no need code can be observed; the need is inferred from what the agency leads with, paid performance first, and the sentence says so. A rival cannot name a contestable account from this record, which is itself the finding: an agency that bills itself the most reviewed in the US publishes reviews, not named work.

No shared clients appear on other tracked agencies' books, the empty result of an empty book rather than loyalty.

What the base needs next, tied to the edition: the sold mix leans on Paid Search and Paid Social, the two lines that drive its KJ4 exposure (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net -0.404), so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that its mid market buyers ask for the inputs automation consumes, first party data, creative volume and measurement, which the record scores partial on P4; and a roughly even chance that the same buyers ask for ads inside AI answers under KJ2, where P8 is absent.
house: Say and do: 2 of 3 tested lines hold. Paid Search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 22 in the Transparency Center and 17 in the last 30 days, advertiser Disruptive Advertising, Inc, last shown 2026-09-27; a sample ends 'Get a free audit today'. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 24+ ads, 20 company ads and 4 thought leader ads, a floor since 503 ads match the name query; one reads 'We've run 2,000+ engagements and the problem is almost never the ads'. Paid Social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site, the one gap flagged. Content velocity: 1,619 sitemap URLs, 22 updated in 90 days and 138 in 365, with 6 AI topic URLs. No llms.txt, and it blocks GPTBot and Google-Extended. The stack is gtm, hubspot, hotjar, vwo and termly on WordPress and Gatsby.
market:
The Horus read: tailwind index 5.8, band Neutral, 32nd percentile, integrity 66.7. Best placed for KJ1 (The click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.269), driven by AI Search / GEO at +2 and Paid Search at +1, and for KJ2 (ads inside AI answers, net 0.269). Most exposed to KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net -0.404), Paid Search and Paid Social at -2 each. Best fit: The Walled Oasis at 50/100. P moves: making P5 (outcome pricing); partial on P1, P4 and P7; absent on P2, P3, P6 and P8.

The Monsoon read: index 52.1, band Breeze, 36th percentile, migration 52.1 and displacement 52.1 level. The verdict puts 52 of the index on the sold mix, Paid Search (14) and SEO (7) carrying the most movable hours, sends 65% of the work to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, and notes automation overlaps 37% of the movable hours. The class is observed on the outcome pricing term; no hub office and no onshore claim are listed.
openings:
The contradiction to lead with is observed: it sells Paid Social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival who puts that beside the 4.8 Clutch average wins the paid social line, since the record gives Disruptive no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth to answer with (P4 partial). The falsifier: a social ad pixel on disruptiveadvertising.com at the next compile.

Second, the AI line. It blocks GPTBot and Google-Extended while selling AI visibility at blog depth (P1 partial) and shows no sign of ads inside AI assistants (P8 absent): it is very likely, with high confidence, that Disruptive is not that agency on this record.

Third, price. Its outcome offer, results within 90 days or no fee for qualifying brands, is an unusually explicit pricing signal and the one thing a rival must match rather than undercut; the contestable ground is the KJ4 exposure, Paid Search and Paid Social at -2, where a rival selling the inputs automation runs on has a roughly even chance of taking accounts an audit first pitch cannot hold.
watch: I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: disclosed AI checkout GMV would deepen the KJ4 exposure on its paid search and paid social hours, while high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, while growth above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and its KJ1 tailwind.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and any pricing below $20 CPM would change the KJ2 read on its paid search line, where P8 is absent.
No dated move sits in the record; the items to follow are whether a named client or case study appears and whether the GPTBot and Google-Extended blocks are lifted.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients, and this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
